title: Julian Dehne
text:
After completing a BA in European Studies at the University of Passau, I sought to enhance my background with expertise in Computer Science. The dual subject teacher program in Brandenburg and Berlin uniquely offered a combination of Political Science and Computer Science, which aligned perfectly with my interests. During my stay at the University of Potsdam, I had the privilege of working under Professor Ulrike Lucke, a leading figure in e-learning research in Germany.
Following my PhD, I briefly joined Humboldt University in Berlin, where I co-authored one of the first conceptual papers on fostering creativity through e-learning. Subsequently, I decided to return to my roots in the social sciences, accepting a PostDoc position at the University of Göttingen in the CSS field. Here, our team has been developing an innovative chatbot designed to facilitate deliberation on social media, which is nearing operational functionality.

title: Software
text:
An open-source framework for annotating research code in empirical software-engineering studies, used in my corpus work on what research software a community actually produces. rse-code-annotations is MIT-licensed.



At GESIS, I am responsible for developing a platform that consolidates open educational resources (OER) focused on data quality. The KODAQS TOOLBOX employs a sophisticated transformation pipeline, enabling OER to be created independently on GitHub using various technology stacks while preserving a cohesive look and feel across a unified website.



In Göttingen Valentin Gold and me developed a toolchain that can download live discussions on social media to be presented for human-in-the-loop coders. This allowed us to test different moderation strategies for the chatbot to improve social media discussion.




While in Potsdam, I developed a pioneering concept on the persistence of learning outcomes and its applications. However, encountering challenges in mainstreaming the COMPBASE (not public) platform for testing, I redirected my thesis toward Inquiry-Based Learning.

title: About Me
text:
Work
Following my PhD, I accepted a PostDoc position at the University of Göttingen in the Computational Social Science field. Here, our team has developed a chatbot that can moderate social media discussions trying to make them more deliberative. Unfortunately, Twitter/Musk crashed the scientific experiment in the middle of its lifespan. After that I have worked as a Research Software Engineer with GESIS, and now I am orchestrating the effort to pilot a master curriculum for Research Software Engineering.

title: Current Work
text:
Group Lead for Research Software Engineering at the German Informatics Society (GI), holding the scientific direction of the FG RSE
Directing the Master Curriculum Research Software Engineering (RSE-Master 2025), and representing that work in the Skills and Training for Research Software (STaRS) Forum of the Research Software Alliance
Project lead of the GI RSE Award for outstanding research software, and PI for the GI in FutuRSI (Future of Sustainable Research Software Infrastructure)
Writing a habilitation on methodological research integrity for research software (the RIGHT framework); first chapter available as a preprint
Teaching RSE as a guest lecturer at RWTH Aachen, with two further RSE courses at the University of Potsdam in the coming semester
Paper projects with the teaching RSE group of deRSE
